newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Texaco predicts higher dividend.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Texaco predicts higher dividend.

text.p: Petroleum products marketer Texaco Nigeria on Friday said it would pay an improved dividend once its new product terminal became operational.
"We will pay higher dividends since the terminal will become operational soon," , managing director Tom Hauck told journalists in Lagos.
In June Texaco said it paid 450 million naira from internal funds for the depot and its refurbishment. Consequently, no dividends were paid to shareholders for the year ended December 1995.
The terminal will free the company from a current sharing arrangement with one of its rivals, an option it says affects earnings tremendously.
"We have already started test-running at the terminal. By the time we consolidate our operations, our shareholders shall smile," Hauck said.
Profits at Nigerian petroleum marketing companies have fallen recently on insufficient supply of products and stiff competition from independent marketers.
Hauck said low margins from state-fixed prices further worsened their financial performances.
"The present margin of 1.30 naira (on every litre of fuel) allowed us is not enough to offset operating costs; marketers have already recommended an increase," he said.
Texas Petroleum Company has a 60 percent stake in Texaco Nigeria, with Nigerian investors holding the balance.
